subject: Renal
vignette: A renal biopsy from a 38-year-old man with nephrotic-range proteinuria shows sclerosis affecting only some of the glomeruli; the majority appear normal. The pathologist reports that fewer than half of the sampled glomeruli are involved, with segmental scarring in those affected.
question: Which term correctly describes this pattern of glomerular involvement?

options.text: Diffuse, because more than 50% of glomeruli are involved
Proliferative, because the glomeruli are hypercellular
Focal, because fewer than 50% of glomeruli are involved
Membranous, because the GBM is thickened
Secondary, because a systemic disease is the cause

explanation_correct: In renal pathology, focal means involvement of fewer than 50% of glomeruli, and the classic example is focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), in which only some glomeruli show segmental scarring. Diffuse is reserved for involvement of more than half of glomeruli, as in diffuse proliferative glomerulonephritis. This distinction describes the extent of disease rather than the cellular or membranous pattern.

explanation_incorrect.A: Diffuse involvement means more than 50% of glomeruli are affected; this biopsy shows the opposite.
explanation_incorrect.B: Proliferative refers to hypercellularity within glomeruli, not to the proportion of glomeruli involved.
explanation_incorrect.D: Membranous describes thickening of the glomerular basement membrane, which is not what is described here.
explanation_incorrect.E: Secondary denotes a systemic cause of glomerular disease, a separate classification axis from focal versus diffuse.

educationalObjective: Focal glomerular disease involves fewer than 50% of glomeruli, exemplified by FSGS.

subject: Renal
vignette: A 55-year-old woman with nephrotic syndrome undergoes kidney biopsy. Electron microscopy shows thickening of the glomerular basement membrane with subepithelial deposits, and light microscopy shows diffuse capillary wall thickening. No significant hypercellularity is present.
question: Which nomenclature term is defined by thickening of the glomerular basement membrane?

options.text: Membranous
Focal
Proliferative
Diffuse
Primary

explanation_correct: Membranous refers to thickening of the glomerular basement membrane, the defining feature of membranous nephropathy, a common cause of nephrotic syndrome in adults. The biopsy described shows diffuse GBM thickening with subepithelial immune deposits and relatively little inflammation. This is distinct from proliferative patterns, in which hypercellularity dominates.

explanation_incorrect.B: Focal refers to the proportion of glomeruli involved, specifically fewer than 50%, not to GBM thickening.
explanation_incorrect.C: Proliferative denotes hypercellular glomeruli, which are absent in this biopsy.
explanation_incorrect.D: Diffuse describes involvement of more than 50% of glomeruli and does not specify the type of lesion.
explanation_incorrect.E: Primary indicates a kidney-specific disease rather than a morphologic pattern.

educationalObjective: Membranous glomerular disease is defined by thickening of the glomerular basement membrane.

subject: Renal
vignette: A biopsy from a patient with nephritic-nephrotic syndrome shows glomeruli that are markedly hypercellular with increased mesangial and endothelial cells, accompanied by splitting of the basement membrane producing a 'tram-track' appearance on PAS stain.
question: Which term in glomerular disease nomenclature specifically denotes hypercellular glomeruli?

options.text: Membranous
Focal
Secondary
Diffuse
Proliferative

explanation_correct: Proliferative glomerular disease means the glomeruli are hypercellular, as seen in membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (MPGN). The increased cellularity reflects proliferation of mesangial and endothelial cells together with influx of inflammatory cells. In this vignette the hypercellularity plus GBM splitting, or tram-tracking, is the classic MPGN picture.

explanation_incorrect.A: Membranous disease is defined by GBM thickening, not by increased cell number.
explanation_incorrect.B: Focal describes the fraction of glomeruli involved, fewer than 50%, not hypercellularity.
explanation_incorrect.C: Secondary refers to glomerular injury from a systemic disease, a different classification axis.
explanation_incorrect.D: Diffuse means more than 50% of glomeruli are involved, irrespective of the cellular pattern.

educationalObjective: Proliferative glomerular disease is characterized by hypercellular glomeruli, as in MPGN.

subject: Renal
vignette: A medical student is learning two overlapping ways to classify glomerular disease. One scheme asks whether the process is confined to the kidney itself or is part of a systemic illness; another describes the light-microscopic pattern. The student is given minimal change disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, and diabetic nephropathy as examples.
question: Which of the following correctly pairs a category with its example?

options.text: Secondary glomerular disease — minimal change disease
Primary glomerular disease — minimal change disease
Primary glomerular disease — systemic lupus erythematosus
Secondary glomerular disease — primary focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
Membranous nephropathy — a purely clinical rather than morphologic category

explanation_correct: Primary glomerular disease is a disorder that arises in the kidney itself and specifically affects the glomeruli; minimal change disease is the classic example. Secondary glomerular disease occurs when a systemic disease or a disease of another organ also damages the glomeruli, as with SLE and diabetic nephropathy. Therefore pairing primary with minimal change disease is correct.

explanation_incorrect.A: Minimal change disease is a primary, kidney-specific disorder, not a secondary one.
explanation_incorrect.C: SLE is a systemic autoimmune disease and therefore an example of secondary glomerular disease, not primary.
explanation_incorrect.D: Primary FSGS is a kidney-specific disease; the standard unambiguous teaching example of a primary disease here is minimal change disease.
explanation_incorrect.E: Membranous nephropathy is defined by a morphologic feature, namely GBM thickening, so it is not a purely clinical category.

educationalObjective: Primary glomerular disease is kidney-specific (eg, minimal change disease); secondary disease results from systemic illness (eg, SLE, diabetes).
